main.name: Goh Jia Yi, Jesa
main.headline: AI Engineer specialising in LLM safety, computer vision, and applied ML systems.
bio: Hi, I’m Jia Yi — I also go by Jesa!

I’m currently exploring the realm of Responsible AI to make AI products safer and more trustworthy for public use. The unprecedented pace of AI advancements makes waking up each day exciting, but it also reinforces the need to build responsibly, which is what keeps me up at night (in a good way).
Transforming ideas into tangible working solutions brings me joy.

education.degree: Bachelor of Science (BSc.) in Business Analytics
activities: ML Tech Lead, NUS FinTech Society

work.title: Applied Research Scientist, Responsible AI
description: Led the research and development of safety testing frameworks for government LLM applications, covering taxonomy and benchmark construction, automated judging methods, and quantitative scoring for chatbots.
Operationalised research findings into evaluation tools and platform capabilities now used by over 10 agency users across the government.
Published technical papers formalising frameworks, contributing to broader adoption of safety evaluation standards, with publications accepted as oral spotlight at the ICML 2025 TAIG workshop.

work.title: AI Engineer, Video Analytics
description: Led end-to-end development of 7+ applied ML systems as the primary engineer, designing bespoke pipelines across diverse use cases such as autonomous robot safety monitoring and contactless vital sign extraction.
Built and refined solutions across a diverse range of model architectures, including conventional computer vision, transformers-based, and vision-language models.
Deployed models on the Government Commercial Cloud, including packaging, implementing inference logic, and ensuring stable, secure, real-time performance for downstream users.
Collaborated with government agencies, research institutions, and industry partners to co-develop ML solutions from initial scoping through final deployment.

work.title: Machine Learning Engineer Intern
description: Designed and deployed document processing components for HR workflows, automating document classification and quality assessment with 96% precision while enhancing robustness through quality enhancement methods.
Improved information extraction performance to 92% accuracy by running regression tests, identifying error patterns, and refining NLP classification and extraction models.

work.title: Machine Learning Engineer Intern
description: Developed an exercise detection and rep counting computer vision application aimed at streamlining Individual Physical Proficiency Test (IPPT) processes.

items.title: Safety Testing Framework for LLM Applications
items.summary: A safety testing framework for government LLM applications, covering risk taxonomy design, benchmark construction, automated judging methods, and quantitative scoring tailored for real-world chatbot deployments. Presented as an oral spotlight at the ICML 2025 Workshop on Technical AI Governance.

items.title: Autonomous Ground Robot Monitoring for Safety Breach Detection
items.summary: A real-time safety monitoring system for autonomous ground robots, combining classical CV and transformer-based perception models to detect safety barrier breaches in challenging outdoor environments. Includes a monitoring dashboard that surfaces safety triggers for on-site operators to visualise alerts.

items.title: Contactless Vital Sign Extraction with Remote Photoplethysmography (rPPG)
items.summary: Built a contactless rPPG vital-sign estimation system from facial video, delivering accurate heart-rate and respiration estimates, with experimental modelling for blood-pressure prediction. Led the pipeline across dataset design, signal processing, and ML model development.

items.title: 1st Runner-up, Shopee Ultra Hackathon
items.summary: Built a standalone mobile application prototype within 36 hours, integrating Shopee's APIs to deliver new engagement-focused user experiences. Designed and engineered the app using React Native and secured 1st runner-up among 96 competing teams.
